analysis.investment_thesis: KRBL trades cheaply (EV/EBITDA 6.7x, earnings yield ~8.1%) but its ROIC of ~11.8% falls well short of the Magic Formula's 20%+ threshold for a genuinely good business. With both earnings yield and ROIC below my buy criteria, and a contracting profitability trend, this is a mediocre business at a mediocre price — not a Magic Formula pick.
key_strengths: India Gate brand — dominant basmati franchise with global exports providing some pricing power
Near-zero debt (D/E 0.01) and INR 5,460 Cr reserves; balance sheet is fortress-like
Low capex intensity (INR 96 Cr capex vs INR 754 Cr EBITDA in 2025 = ~13%) — business doesn't require heavy reinvestment
key_risks: ROIC ~11.8% — well below Magic Formula's 20% threshold; this is a commodity-adjacent business that can't earn exceptional returns on capital
Contracting EBITDA trend: peaked at INR 1,021 Cr in 2023, fell to INR 754 Cr in 2025 (-26%) — margin compression is real
Lumpy, volatile cash flows (FCF swung from -INR 419 Cr in 2023 to +INR 866 Cr in 2025) driven by paddy inventory cycles
red_flags: 9-year revenue CAGR of only 5.8% — barely above Indian inflation; no pricing power moat
Operating income CAGR of 4.7% trails revenue growth, signaling structural margin erosion
Other Income of INR 61–97 Cr materially flatters net profit — 2025 PAT (INR 476 Cr) looks optically cheap partly because of non-operating items
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: **Earnings Yield = EBIT/EV = INR 674 Cr / INR 8,288 Cr ≈ 8.1%** — above the 6% floor but short of my 12% "attractive" threshold. **ROIC = EBIT / Capital Employed ≈ 674 / 5,736 Cr ≈ 11.8%** — confirmed by the stated ROCE of 11.80%. Both metrics land in "adequate but uninspiring" territory. The Magic Formula requires top-decile ranking on BOTH dimensions; KRBL clears neither bar. At EV/EBITDA of 6.7x and forward P/E of 9.4x the stock looks statistically cheap, but cheapness alone is a value trap without the high-ROIC engine to compound returns.

The deeper problem is structural: basmati rice is a semi-commodity where scale provides some advantage but not the durable pricing power needed to sustain 20%+ ROIC. EBITDA peaked in FY23 at INR 1,021 Cr and has contracted for two consecutive years to INR 754 Cr in FY25 — a 26% decline. Revenue is growing (5.8% CAGR) but profitability is not keeping pace, which is the opposite of what the Magic Formula wants to see. The fortress balance sheet (D/E 0.01) and the India Gate brand are genuine assets, making this a capital-safe HOLD for existing shareholders, but not a buy for a return-on-capital focused strategy.
